title: Panel Optimization for High-Dimensional Immunophenotyping Assays Using Full-Spectrum Flow Cytometry
protocol: Check the quality of acquired SRCs.
Evaluate spectral mismatches between beads and cells for each fluorophore using N × N plots.
Assess unmixing accuracy on actual sample (cells) to be used in the assay.
Determine optimum SRCs (cells or beads) for future unmixing.
Thaw PBMCs quickly in a 37°C water bath and add to 5 ml PBS with 2% FBS.
Centrifuge the mixture for 5 minutes at 500 × g at room temperature, then carefully flick off the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in PBS with 2% FBS and count viable cells on a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge as before and carefully flick off the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in PBS with 2% FBS to achieve a concentration of 5 × 10^6 viable cells/ml.
Distribute 100 μl cell suspension per well into a 96-well U-bottom plate, allocating one well for each fluorophore in the panel and one well for an unstained sample.
Add one drop of vortexed compensation beads to a second set of wells.
Mix with 150 μl FACs staining buffer in each well.
Allocate one well per fluorophore in the panel except for the viability dye.
Include unstained and FS sample wells in the plate setup.
Prepare two wells per fluorophore: one with cells and one with compensation beads.
Incorporate FMO controls where marker expression is very low or dim.
Centrifuge plate 5 min at 500 × g, 4°C.
Flick off the supernatant.
Prepare viability stain in PBS according to the titration result.
Add 100 μl of viability stain to the live/dead cell control and FS sample.
Resuspend remaining wells with 100 μl PBS.
Incubate for 15-30 min at room temperature, protected from light.
Centrifuge as above and flick off the supernatant.
Block Fc receptors using 100 μl of 1:40 Fc block in FACS staining buffer.
Add an equal volume of FACS staining buffer to the beads.
Incubate for 10 min at 4°C.
Centrifuge as above and flick off the supernatant.
Centrifuge antibody stocks for 5 minutes at 16,000-18,000 × g at 4°C.
Filter antibody stocks using a pore size of 0.1-0.65 μm.
Dilute SS, FS, and FMO control antibody mixes in FACS staining buffer according to titration results.
Pipette from the top of the liquid to avoid centrifuged aggregates.
Prepare enough volume of each antibody mix for two samples per mix.
Make excess antibody mix to account for pipetting errors (n + 1).
Add Brilliant Stain Buffer Plus when using more than one Brilliant polymer dye simultaneously, following manufacturer's instructions.
Do not add Brilliant Stain Buffer Plus to compensation beads.
Stain all cells and beads with 100 μl of the appropriate antibody mix in the dark.
Incubate according to the final assay conditions.
Centrifuge samples and flick off the supernatant.
Wash samples twice with 200 μl FACS staining buffer.
Centrifuge again after each wash.
Resuspend cells in 200 μl FACS staining buffer if required for biosafety or sample longevity.
Acquire samples on a Cytek Aurora, ensuring scatter profiles of cells and beads are on scale.
Optimize the FSC area scaling factor (ASF) for instrument setup.
Ensure all fluorescence signals are on scale (<4 × 10^6).
Record all tubes with the same fluorescence gain settings for each detector.
Collect at least 300 events for each positive and negative population.
For bead controls, record a minimum of 5000 total events.
For cell controls, record between 30,000 to 50,000 total events or more if necessary to obtain at least 300 positive events with similar fluorescence intensity.
Evaluate results using SpectroFlo software.
Check the raw reference control data in SpectroFlo.
Verify that scatter profiles of cells and beads are on-scale, clean, and easily gated.
Confirm that FSC ASF has been optimized.
Use Cytek assay settings or a close alteration as discussed in Critical Parameters for Complex Samples.
Ensure all tubes have been recorded with the same settings.
Check that the unstained sample has no contamination from other fluorophores.
In the SpectroFlo software, step through the Unmixing Wizard and select beads for all SRCs except unstained and viability controls.
Accurately place positive and negative gates for unmixing.
Set the scatter gate on the smaller-sized or more abundant singlet population when setting scatter gates on bead SRCs.
Verify that peaks seen in staining level are not due to contaminating fluorophores or sample carryover.
Optimize the staining procedure where needed to achieve homogenous staining intensity across all positive beads.
Perform quality control of all spectral signatures by verifying peak channel matches defined in Cytek's Full Spectrum Viewer.
Check that the spectral signature appears as expected based on guidelines and historical data from Cytek.
Ensure each channel contains a tight population of events.
Confirm all fluorescent signals are on-scale (<4 × 106) in full-spectrum plots or individual detector plots.
Record sufficient events to find a clear positive signal.
Place the positive gate over the negative population for each fluorophore to verify no fluorophore contamination.
Check Similarity Indices under the QC Controls tab to ensure all spectral signatures are unique (i.e., values within the matrix are ≤0.98).
Select the Live Unmix button to generate unmixed FCS files.
Create N × N plots on an unmixed worksheet using software such as FlowJo or FCS Express.
Create pseudocolor or dot plots for each fluorophore in the panel, ensuring all x axes are set to the same fluorophore and y axes to different fluorophores.
Change x and y axes from manual scaling to autoscaling in plot properties.
Save this workspace as a template for use in later protocol steps.
Select the first SS cell sample.
Select all N × N plots.
In the Plot Properties window, change the x-axis option to the fluorophore matching the selected sample so all plots change simultaneously.
Evaluate the unmixing accuracy of the marker on the x axis by visually inspecting whether the positive and negative populations are well aligned horizontally along the x axis.
Make a note of which control was being viewed if unmixing errors are seen in the N × N matrix plots.
Repeat steps 29-31 until the unmixing of all fluorophores has been evaluated.
Note which fluorophores require cells to be used for the SRC (i.e., those with identified unmixing errors).
All other controls can remain as beads.
Go through the Unmixing Wizard a second time using the controls identified in step 33 as the optimal controls.
Unmix again using live unmixing.
Follow steps 23-26 for the modified controls to ensure the best unmixing outcome is achieved.
When setting gates using cells as SRCs, place the scatter gate only on the cells expressing the marker of interest for each control.
In cases where there is no negative staining in this population, use a universal negative as a surrogate.
Compare the observed negative signal to the matching unstained tube to ensure it is due to AF rather than contamination.
Repeat steps 29-32 to evaluate the new unmixing for the fluorophores that did not unmix optimally before.
Note which fluorophores require cells or beads to be used for the SRC.
Thaw cryopreserved PBMCs in PBS containing 10% FBS.
Incubate thawed PBMCs in Zombie NIR Fixable Viability Kit reagent for viability staining according to manufacturer's instructions.
Wash stained cells twice with FACS staining buffer.
Block Fc receptors on the surface of PBMCs using Human TruStain FcX solution.
Incubate PBMCs with antibodies targeting specific functional markers as indicated in Table 1.
Wash antibody-labeled PBMCs twice with FACS staining buffer.
Resuspend PBMCs in FACS staining buffer for analysis.
Thaw PBMCs quickly in a 37°C water bath.
Add thawed PBMCs to 5 ml PBS with 2% FBS.
Centrifuge the sample for 5 min at 500 × g, room temperature.
Carefully flick off the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend cells in PBS with 2% FBS and count on a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge as before and carefully flick off the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in PBS with 2% FBS to a concentration of 5 × 10^6 cells/ml.
Distribute 100 μl cell suspension per well of a 96-well U-bottom plate.
Allocate six wells for each antibody being titrated.
Include additional wells for unstained and live/dead controls.
Centrifuge plate 5 min at 500 × g, 4°C, and flick off the supernatant.
Stain titration samples and live/dead controls with a viability dye that will not cause significant spillover into the fluorophore being titrated.
Centrifuge as above and flick off the supernatant.
Block Fc receptors by applying 100 μl of a 1:40 dilution of Human TruStain FcX and incubating 10 min at 4°C.
Add one drop of vortexed compensation beads per well for the appropriate single stain (SS) controls.
Centrifuge as above and flick off the supernatant.
Remove aggregates from antibody stocks by centrifuging vials for 5 minutes at 16,000-18,000 × g at 4°C.
Alternatively, filter the antibody stocks using a pore size of 0.65 μm or smaller.
Create a dilution series for each antibody being titrated in FACS staining buffer.
Pipette from the top of the liquid to avoid spun-down aggregates when preparing dilutions.
Dilute stock solutions at suggested concentrations: 1:50, 1:100, 1:200, 1:400, 1:800, and 1:1600.
Add 100 μl of each antibody dilution to the corresponding sample in the plate.
Add FACS staining buffer to unstained and live/dead controls.
Use 100 μl of a 1:100 dilution for compensation beads.
Incubate using the time and temperature that will be used in the final assay.
Centrifuge as above and flick off the supernatant.
Wash twice with 200 μl FACS staining buffer.
If fixation will be used for the final samples, determine titrations using fixed samples.
Resuspend in 200 μl FACS staining buffer.
Acquire on a Cytek Aurora using Cytek assay settings.
Open titration samples in data analysis software for analyzing FCS files.
Generate median fluorescence intensity (MdFI) values for positive and negative populations for each concentration.
Generate standard deviation (SD) values for the negative population for each concentration.
Calculate the stain index (SI) using the equation SI = (MdnFIpos – MdnFIneg) / (2 × SDneg).
Select the concentration that gives rise to the best stain index without causing a positive shift in the negative population.
Observe which fluorescent channel(s) has an off-scale signal.
Adjust fluorescent gain settings carefully to minimize impact on all spectral signatures within the panel.
Reduce whole detector arrays simultaneously for all detectors of a given laser line.
Check changes using Cytek's Full Spectrum Viewer, published fluorophore guidelines, or historical data.
Determine the gain setting using trial and error to bring the emission peak on-scale (i.e., <4 × 106 on the Aurora).
Reduce secondary detector arrays by the same percentage as the reduction made in the gain setting.

Use Cytek's Full Spectrum Viewer, published fluorophore guidelines, or historical data to check that the altered spectral signature retains the correct overall pattern and primary emission peak has not been reduced below any secondary emission peaks.
If the overall pattern is incorrect, continue adjusting other laser lines by reducing their respective detector arrays by the same percentage as in step 2.
Repeat steps 4 and 5 until the spectral signature appears as expected or all arrays have been reduced by the same percentage.
Record all samples at the adjusted settings.
Check the FS sample for clean data by removing artefacts such as doublets, dead cells, and aggregates.
Verify positive staining for all markers in the panel, considering the biology of each marker.
Determine if the selected SRCs (beads or cells) successfully unmix the SS cells from Basic Protocol 1.
Evaluate whether the selected SRCs can also successfully unmix the FS sample.
Use FCS files generated in Basic Protocol 1 for evaluation.
Utilize N × N worksheet template for analysis.
Work through the Unmixing Wizard in SpectroFlo software and select the SRCs chosen from Basic Protocol 1.
In the unmixed workspace, gate on time to remove events collected during an unstable flow period by plotting time vs. scatter (e.g., FSC-A or FSC-H).
Gate out doublets by plotting FSC-H vs. FSC-A.
Gate out doublets by plotting SSC-H vs. SSC-A.
Include only the events found in the diagonal population for doublet exclusion.
Exclude unlysed erythrocytes from whole blood or PBMC samples using the blue/violet SSC gating method.
Inspect N × N plots for incorrectly unmixed super-bright events to exclude aggregates.
Gate out dead cells by including only viability dye negative events.
Gate on cells of interest using FSC-A vs. SSC-A, including only required events for analysis.
Include only the cells that will be involved in downstream analysis.
Create pseudocolor or dot plots for each fluorophore in the panel.
Set the y axis to SSC-A and each x axis to a different fluorophore.
Verify that a positive signal can be found for all markers.
Use FMOs to determine gating boundaries for rare or dim markers if necessary.
Take note of reagents with no clear signal and check their titer and staining protocol.
Open the N × N worksheet template.
Evaluate how well unmixing was performed for each marker.
Inspect the FS sample by assessing whether super-negative events are present.
Select all plots making up the matrix.
In the Plot Properties window, change the x axis option to the next fluorophore down the list so that all plots change simultaneously.
Repeat steps until all fluorophores have been checked.
If there are no major unmixing errors, continue to evaluation of marker resolution.
If there are unmixing issues, make small adjustments (<3%) to the compensation matrix found in the Tube Properties window.
Adjustments to the spillover matrix should be fully justified.
Ensure the integrity of the data is not impacted by adjustments.
Manually adjust under-unmixing and over-unmixing issues if necessary.
Limit manual corrections to no more than 2% to 3%.
Re-evaluate unmixing accuracy if greater correction is needed.
Test AF extraction to determine if marker resolution can be improved.
Create a histogram for each fluorophore in the panel.
If the positive population is rare, use a dot plot instead of a histogram.
Overlay the same number of FS and SS cell sample events onto a histogram.
Overlay the same number of FS and SS cell sample events onto a dot plot.
Downsample the cells of interest population from all samples to the same number of events based on the sample with the fewest cells of interest.
Select the population of interest in FlowJo.
Go to the Workspace tab.
Select Plugins and then DownSample.
Specify the number of events for downsampling.
Determine whether spreading of the negative population has occurred in the FS sample.
Determine whether such spreading has impacted the resolution of positive and negative populations, either visually or by calculating stain index (SI).
Create a spillover spreading matrix (SSM) to assess which fluorophores are likely to be introducing spread to the fluorophore of interest.
Using SS cells SRCs in FlowJo, navigate through the Compensation Wizard defining positive and negative populations for each fluorophore.
The SSM will be automatically generated alongside the compensation matrix.
Display or export the SSM from the SSM button.
Investigate any reduction in positive signal.
Refer to Jalbert, Shikuma, Ndhlovu, & Barbour (2013) and Park et al. (2020) for explanations.
Apply sequential staining of chemokine receptors if necessary to achieve a positive signal comparable to that of the SS cell controls.
Sequential staining can also be applied to non-chemokine receptors.
Open SpectroFlo and proceed to the Unmixing Wizard.
Test unmixing without AF extraction first, selecting live unmixing.
Repeat steps of the Unmixing Wizard with AF extraction, placing the scatter gate on the population of interest only.
Select Unmix, Save & Open to generate a separate set of FCS files.
If there are other cells of interest in the sample that have a brighter spectral signature, try to unmix with the scatter gate on this population.
Determine the best unmixing outcome by comparing N × N plots and evaluating changes in resolution for overlapping dyes.
Observe N × N plot permutations of raw channel data on the Aurora.
Draw pseudocolor or dot plots for each channel permutation, setting each y axis to different channels.
Find a combination that separates the greatest number of populations from one another.
Choose the plot with the highest degree of separation.
Place gates around all unique populations and observe scatter properties and spectral signatures on adjacent plots.
Find the peak fluorescent channel for each unique population.
Display each population on a histogram using its peak channel.
Gate the brightest 300-500 cells to derive the brightest AF SS control.
Right-click on the gate and export events as a new FCS file.
Repeat for all unique populations, producing an FCS file for each.
Export an AF dim population to be used as the negative control.
Designate these new AF signatures as fluorescence tags in the SpectroFlo Library.
Create a new AF group to facilitate filtering and exporting fluorophores.
Assign the excitation laser and emission wavelength based on peak emission channel.
Open the experiment of interest and add the new AF tag(s) as if it were a fluorophore.
In the reference controls tab, add an additional negative for the AF tags.
Import the populations exported during the Distinguish steps as SRCs for the corresponding tags.
Import the AF dim population as an additional negative for the AF SRCs.
Use the Unmixing Wizard QC tools to assess AF signature similarity.
Unmix the experiment and evaluate the unmixed N × N matrix.
Perform expert gating using data analysis software.
Analyze FCS files generated in Basic Protocol 3.
Use t-SNE analysis with 1000 iterations and perplexity of 30 for quality control.
Display t-SNE analysis in 2D plots using resultant dimensions.
Visualize expression levels of HLA-DR, CD27, CD28, CD45RA, CRTH2, CD127, TCRγδ, CD4, CCR4, CCR6, CD45RO, CD25, CCR10, CD8, CCR7, PLZF, CTLA-4, MR1tet, FoxP3, and CXCR3.
Use a rainbow heat scale to visualize t-SNE scales.
Open the unmixed FS sample in data analysis software.
Follow steps 2-6 of Basic Protocol 2 to gate on live single cells of interest.
Gate the rest of the markers based on panel design, prior knowledge, and published literature.
Check the gating strategy for unexpected marker combinations or cell populations.
Evaluate whether all populations of interest have clear positive signals that can be easily resolved from the negative.
Ensure readout markers can be quantified in each of the cell types of interest.
Apply a dimensionality reduction algorithm (t-SNE).
Run t-SNE at default settings (iterations: 1000; perplexity: 30) utilizing all fluorescence parameters.
Exclude non-informative parameters such as viability and phenotypic markers for identifying cells of interest.
Assess marker co-localization one by one in viSNE plots.
Color the t-SNE based on the expression of each marker.
Check for unexpected marker combinations on specific cell types.
